pr_body:
Epic: CRDB-23559
Informs #98431. 
Fixes #94856.
(Based off #98459)
Supersedes #98380.

This change introduces a mechanism through which an operator can
select a "configuration profile" via the command-line flag
`--config-profile` or env var `COCKROACH_CONFIG_PROFILE`. The SQL
initialization defined by the profile is applied during server
start-up.

The profiles are (currently) hardcoded inside CockroachDB.

The following profiles are predefined:

- `default`: no configuration.

- `multitenant+noapp`: no pre-defined `application` tenant, but with a
  predefined application tenant template that is used whenever a new
  tenant is defined. This config profile is meant for use for C2C
  replication target clusters.

- `multitenant+app+sharedservice`: shared-process multitenancy with
  pre-defined `application` tenant, based off the same configuration as
  `multitenant+noapp`.

Release note: None

issue_context.title: server: separate config defaults for serverless vs dedicated/SH secondary tenants
issue_context.body:
We've discovered a number of configuration / tuning knobs which we want to be different when running multi-tenancy in CC dedicated / self-hosted, vs in Serverless. (partial list below)

There should be a convenient way to initialize a secondary tenant with one set of defaults vs another.

A proposal on the table is to use "tenant templates" (like pg already has db templates).

Partial list (not exhaustive):

- tenant name
- special capabilities
- cluster settings
  - `spanconfig.tenant_limit`
  - `kv.tenant_rate_limiter.*`
  - `spanconfig.tenant_coalesce_adjacent.enabled` (maybe)
  - `sql.schema.test_object_generator.enabled`
  - `sql.distsql.direct_columnar_scans.enabled` (being introduced in #94438)
    - helps all TPC-H queries with shared process multitenancy
    - some microbenchmarks (less data processed) can get 5-10% slowdown (30% worst case)
    - seems to be most useful for OLAP-y (query accesses multiple rows, fewer columns per row than the table schema)

Jira issue: CRDB-23191
Epic: CRDB-23559
comments:
Hi @ajstorm, please add branch-* labels to identify which branch(es) this release-blocker affects.

<sub>:owl: Hoot! I am a [Blathers](https://github.com/apps/blathers-crl), a bot for [CockroachDB](https://github.com/cockroachdb). My owner is [dev-inf](https://github.com/orgs/cockroachdb/teams/dev-inf).</sub>

Summary of RFC (pending creation of the RFC PR)

> We propose a config mechanism such that clusters intended for different purposes can receive different initial configurations. We need this because various parameters related to multi-tenancy are different in CC Dedicated / SH ("unified architecture") from CC Serverless.
>
> From the outset (from the operator's perspective), the visible tuning knob will be a single env var which switches between a couple of "configuration profiles" that will be hardcoded in the v23.1 release.
>
> Internally, we will be laying the foundations for a more flexible future. This foundation consists of two mechanisms:
>
> - a tenant templating mechanism, by which secondary tenants inherit their properties (incl e.g. capabilities) from a predefined record.
> - a mechanism to inject SQL statements into the startup sequence of the SQL service for any tenant (using the job subsystem).
>
> These internal mechanisms are not exposed directly to end-users in v23.1; they are leveraged together in a fixed manner to create the simple envvar-based tuning knob in v23.1. We will evaluate throughout the v23.x development cycle how much this mechanism could be extended/generalized towards more user-facing features.

Some additional discussion with @arulajmani and then @ajwerner produced the following nuggets of consideration:

- we will want a "ping back" of the job's results from secondary tenants back into the storage cluster, where they can be observed. This will be needed for multi-region serverless, and, we anticipate, for other later use cases.

- we will separate the storage of the "injected SQL statements" from the assignment to specific tenants. Namely, although we want different injected SQL per tenant, we will _also_ want to inject the "same" SQL to all tenants, in a similar way to all-tenant overrides.   So we need (conceptually) 3 relations in our data model:

  - `injected_sql_payloads (payload_id INT, sql_statement STRING)`
  - `injected_sql_definitions(tenant_id INT /* may be 0 for all-tenants */, payload_id INT, sequence_id INT)`
  - `injected_sql_results (tenant_id INT /* may not be zero */, sequence_id INT, completed BOOL, error STRING)` 

  (the latter 2 can be combined into a single table with some elbow grease)

- the `sequence_id` will be used to order the execution of the payloads on each tenant. We agree that the work for a given sequence_id can only start after the work for the previous sequence_id has completed.

- we need a mechanism by which a tenant server cannot observe sequence_id N-1 coming in after it observes sequence_id N.  We can achieve this in various ways. One that appeals to us as a first approach is a monotonicity guarantee on `sequence_id`: if a txn A commits before txn B (regardless of whether A started before or after B), the sequence_id used by A will always be lower than sequence_id used by B.  (i.e. the ordering of sequence_id will follow ordering of txn commit timestamps). We would implement this by computing `max(sequence_id)+1` every time we add a row to the `injected_sql_results` table.

- we will need a tenant connector API to stream all these changes (+ capability changes, + service mode, discussed elsewhere) to tenant servers. For this we have two choices:

  - define multiple streaming RPCs side by side, alongside `TenantSettings`, for example `TenantCapabilities`, `TenantInjectedSQL`, `TenantServiceMode` etc.

  - or, use the single `TenantSettings` endpoint, and extend its result protobuf payload to carry updates to capabilities, service mode and injected SQL as separate sub-types.

  At this point, we are very interested in the latter of these 2 options, because it would allow us to incrementally add the various sub-mechanisms independently from the release process, without violating the rule "no new RPCs in patch releases".  (The alternative is to stub these API endpoints before the 23.1 branch is cut)

- separately, we also need a mechanism to load up a cache of all these values in RAM on every KV node. *Eventually* we can use rangefeeds for all these, but initially a polling solution is acceptable.

  - We noted that one way to simplify the implementation greatly would be to _also_ piggy-back on storing the injeted SQL, *and also* the service mode, *and also* the capabilities, into the `system.tenant_settings` table, so that we have a single rangefeed populating the in-memory cache for all this data.
  - However, given that a polling solution is acceptable as first implementation, we choose instead to use discrete system tables and defer the implementation of rangefeeds over them to a later date.


- we also discussed the problem of "server initialization": we want both the initial setting overrides to be applied (#96512) and the initial SQL to have run before the tenant servers start to accept client traffic.

  - for this, we will make the server initialization wait on the tenant connector to receive the "initial response" from the streaming RPC(s), and apply their results before letting clients connect.

review_comments: If I'm reading the code correctly, the server config is given a NoTaskProvider by default and then the NewProfileSetter will install a new provider _if_ the configuration value is set. 👍
Might be worth noting the obvious: We return a channel that won't see updates because static profiles can't be updated.
We could also enable rangefeed's here so that it can be used as a replication source more easily.
